summary: Big step up from V1 (4.5). The VO fix took the cut from 4:50 to 5:53 (353.1 s, inside 5:30-6:00) with zero VO overlaps. Nothing unmarked runs over 6 s. The climax (B35) is now cut the way the reference cuts action: 7 shots at a 1.2 s mean, flash-in ECUs at 0.9 s, a 1.0 s GFX, then the slow-mo finish. The emotional holds (S066 5.2 s, S067 5.6 s, S068 9.3 s) are marked and have pushes, the default drift is now visible (±30 px, about 86 px of screen travel), and only 5 shots are still locked off. Stats: 116 shots, mean 3.04 s, median 2.67 s, sd 1.34, min 0.90, max 9.29. Histogram: <1.2: 4 | 1.2-2: 12 | 2-3: 55 | 3-5: 32 | 5-6: 11 | 6-9: 1 | >9: 1. In reference bins: <1.5: 8 (7%) | 1.5-3: 63 (54%) | 3-5: 32 | 5-8: 12 | >8: 1. The reference is 25% / 34% / 15% / 13% / 12% (mean 4.46, median 2.42). What holds the score back: (1) the middle is still metronomic. 47% of shots sit in 2-3 s and 16 shots land at exactly 2.2 s, the timeline.js minShot floor. There are only 8 shots under 1.5 s (all in the climax and hall) and only one long moving shot over 8 s, so there's too little contrast between short and long cuts outside B35. (2) The re-angling of the workshop and arena is only partial. S061 is labelled a reverse but shows the same pegboard/window wall, and S067 ('from the doorway') matches the S068 wide almost exactly, which plays as a jump cut into the emotional time-lapse. The hall exchange and the apology still play against one bleacher plate at eye level: S085 'OTS-high' and S089 'LOW' read as eye level, and S102 'WS-low' is a medium two-shot like S099. (3) Pacing inverts at the worst moments. Inside the ticking-clock hall, S085 (4.07 s, static) and S086 (5.2 s) are the two slowest shots of the act, and the B28 robot run S072 is still one 5.85 s track. (4) Five shots are locked off: S084, S085, S089, S102, plus the S080b shake-only insert. Also, the S068 hold is 9.29 s, just over the 9 s cap.

v1_followup.v1_issue: Transitions: only one flash, no whips
v1_followup.note: tin:'flash' on S038, S047, S087, S091b, S094b and S095. tin:'whip' on S036 and S070.

Four new locked-off shots (S084, S085, S089, S102), and three are new V2 angles written with a literal cam object instead of a CAM preset. S071 hides an internal cut (MS → static TELE on Noah at 60%), which then repeats as S082's TELE on Noah 40 s later. S068 is 0.29 s over the hold cap.

strengths: Runtime 5:53 is on target, with zero VO overlaps. Dialogue cuts land on line starts (e.g. S061 cuts in on L043 at -0.05 for the interruption).
The B35 climax is the best-cut sequence in the film: switch → LED flash → sensor GFX → swerve → overhead → 0:01 flash ECU → slow-mo finish, at a 1.2 s mean. That's reference-grade action rhythm.

The emotional spine now breathes. S066 (5.2 s), S067 (5.6 s) and S068 (9.3 s) are marked holds with pushes and in-frame change (DAY counter, light sweep), and B26 averages 6.4 s against 3.2 s for the B24 argument before it.
Camera motion is near-universal: 110/116 shots move. Standouts: S035 lateral dolly 432 px, S072 track 1248 px, S076 POV push z 1→2.13, S082 TELE push, S093 track 1050 px, S104 480 px move.

There's more shot variety: S001b, S043b, S054b, S080b, S091b, S094b and S100b cutaways, the S063 TOP and S065 OTS in the workshop, and S084 geography. The only 3-in-a-row same-type run is the deliberate S002-S004 match chain.
Transitions now follow the reference grammar: 6 flash-ins on power beats and whip-pans into the field and the tournament.

Walk Noah from the BG toward camera, growing h 330→1100, exiting frame-left past the lens. Use CAM.push(1100,560,1.15,1.05,'out') so it pulls out against S068's push-in.
